analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Tracking the rotations across AI and markets post the midterms
key_insights: After the Democrats won the midterms with a larger-than-expected House and Senate majority, markets are focused on political and regulatory uncertainty around energy and the AI/data center buildout. Brent fell over 16% on potential Middle East deescalation, and US equities sold off sharply at the end of last week.

Nasdaq volatility (VXN) had its largest weekly swing since March 2020. Nasdaq implied correlation has risen sharply while average single-stock implied vol also rose, which GS reads as a changing risk regime within US Tech.
US labor data was stronger than expected: NFP +165k, unemployment 4.1% and initial jobless claims at 57-year lows.

The Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) fell to -0.6. Global growth expectations (PC1) weakened and monetary policy (PC2) picked up modestly. All RAI sub-components except bonds and FX are now negative, driven mostly by equity vol and defensive/cyclical factors.
GS's sentiment and positioning indicator fell to its lowest reading since April 2025, so broad positioning is lighter after the selloff.

Historically, RAI readings below -1.5 have preceded stronger S&P 500 returns and lower downside risk, particularly over 6 and 12 months. With the RAI not yet that depressed, the business cycle remains the key anchor for drawdown risk.
Market-based inflation momentum has turned negative with falling energy prices. Weaker growth momentum with more volatility would raise drawdown risk.

As investor focus shifts from AI buildout to monetization, semis have sharply underperformed hyperscalers and KOSPI has underperformed TOPIX. Defensive, value and less AI-dependent areas have outperformed across styles and factors.

GS stays overweight equities over 3m and 12m, citing earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations into year-end. It also stays overweight cash because near-term volatility may linger on AI uncertainty and Middle East tensions.

GS sees three paths to a rebound in risk appetite: easing AI concerns with signs of monetization, rates relief helped by falling energy prices, and a larger decline in the RAI below -1 that improves the asymmetry to add risk.
GS stays overweight bonds and prefers longer duration. Higher yields and peaking nominal growth give a better buffer for equities.

FX strategists see JPY as a complementary hedge against a deeper AI-led sell-off because of its sensitivity to the AI trade. Rates strategists favor payers as an overlay to a long-duration bias, since implied vol historically moderates in the weeks after the midterms.
Cross-asset forecasts: S&P 500 to 8000 at 3m, 8300 at 6m and 8700 at 12m from 7377. US 10-year yield to 4.43% at 12m from 4.86%. Gold to 4,700 at 12m. Brent to 79 and WTI to 71 at 12m.

vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq volatility index (VXN) had its largest weekly swing since March 2020, measured as the sum of absolute 5-day changes.
Nasdaq implied correlation has risen sharply while average single-stock implied vol has risen, pointing to a changing risk regime within US Tech.
S&P 500 3-month implied vol is 17.8 (73rd percentile) against 1-month realised of 20.2 (80th percentile). Nikkei 225 implied vol is 31.1 (98th percentile).
The sentiment and positioning indicator is at its lowest since April 2025, and the RAI equity vol/skew component and defensive factors weighed most on the decline.
Rates strategists favor payers as an overlay to a long-duration bias because implied rate vol historically moderates in the weeks after the midterms.
geopolitical: Potential for deescalation in the Middle East drove Brent down over 16%, though Middle East tensions are still cited as a source of lingering near-term volatility.
Democratic midterm win with a larger-than-expected House and Senate majority is keeping political and regulatory uncertainty around energy and the AI/data center buildout in focus.
